4b57bb9a06: Transposing: every chord moves the same distance
27e129a645: ① Change the chords: move every chord by the same number of semitones. ② Use a capo: keep the shapes, and each fret higher raises it a semitone.
b3e2e4e7ee: Scale degrees are the most useful
0f5a905f95: Remember the song is I–V–vi–IV and you can lay out the chords in any key straight away.
c6cfa7abcb: Move G → D → Em → C into C (down 7 semitones or up 5). What are the chords?
b68c283ca3: I–V–vi–IV in G is still I–V–vi–IV in C: C → G → Am → F.
bf49e98d77: The song is in E and you want to use C shapes. Which fret does the capo go on?
c119245ec0: C → C# → D → D# → E is four semitones, so fret 4. You could also use G shapes at fret 9, but that's very high up.

f2aa0bd1b4: Turn01:05–01:40 Chapter 8: An intro to songwriting
c0b4043d10: Writing a song starts with a story
b73101cb9c: Characters, events, time, place, objects: who the main character is, what happens, when, where, what's left behind. The more specific, the more moving.
5017b17048: Tell your own story as "I", or someone else's as "he" or "she". Point of view decides where the listener stands.
2a428871b3: End lines on words that rhyme (for example the -ou rhyme: 行走, 雙手, 長久), and lyrics flow and stick. You can keep one rhyme throughout or change rhyme between sections.
338302ed9e: The verse tells the story and the chorus makes the point. The song-form map from Chapter 6 works as a framework for writing too.
8153374996: Ideas come and go fast, so record them on your phone as voice memos or notes whenever they come.
1cac66e2f2: Leave it for a day after writing, then sing it to a friend and revise line by line. Most good songs are rewritten again and again.

1e09533882: CloseReference: Chapter 12, caring for an acoustic guitar
ecd9077117: Help your guitar stay with you for years
31e6404d4b: Wipe it clean when changing strings; oil rosewood and ebony fretboards once or twice a year
0573796887: Wipe off sweat with a dry cloth after playing; keep it out of sun, heat and damp
940f384852: Wipe the strings after playing; change them when they sound dull or show rust, roughly every one to two months if you play often
2396f729a7: Humidity around 45–55%; in Taiwan's summer use desiccant packs or a dry cabinet
1a98f0153b: Phosphor bronze: warm and durable, the most common. 80/20 bronze: bright, but dulls faster. Coated strings: smooth feel and longer life, at a higher price.
d03fdca689: Change one string at a time → fix the ball end with the bridge pin → leave two or three frets' length to wind round the peg → wind in one direction → tune, gently stretch the string, and tune again.
